headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI’s shared workspace state can conflict with other agents, while prompt-injection and leakage are limited by the pair’s mostly read-only, vendor-hosted surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel or runtime surface beyond docs, so it cannot directly ingest B. B has shared workspace state and file access, but no clipboard/MCP or shell. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or workspace content, making injection possible but limited.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies A-generated text into B as instructions
IF B is pointed at workspace pages containing attacker-controlled text
mitigations: Use a human review step before pasting A output into B
Strip instruction-like text from copied content
Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Disable any workflow that auto-promotes pasted text into tasks
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to copied content

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read workspace pages and sends content to Notion vendor backends; A is docs-only and touches no data classes, so the main leakage path is from shared workspace content into B’s external calls. Because A lacks filesystem or data access, it is not the source of leakage, but the pair still exposes workspace data through B by default.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are available to the invoking user
IF B is used on pages containing secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Restrict B to non-sensitive pages
Move secrets to a separate workspace
Review Notion AI usage settings
Redact sensitive fields before querying
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B has shared workspace state across instances, but its write_filesystem and modify_git_state are false, reducing conflict to overlapping edits inside Notion-managed content rather than OS-level corruption.
conditions: IF multiple B instances edit the same workspace page concurrently
IF the operator treats A output as a source for manual edits into B
mitigations: Stagger edits to shared pages
Use page-level ownership conventions
Keep one B session per page
Export before bulk edits
requires-engineering: add locking or merge conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so A’s curated list can become an input source that B may summarize or act on without independent verification. A is not authoritative by itself, but B’s default grounding makes downstream over-trust plausible in normal use.
conditions: IF A-derived content is pasted into a Notion page used by B
IF B is asked to summarize or operationalize A-sourced recommendations
mitigations: Mark A-derived content as unverified
Require source links in B outputs
Ask B to cite the originating page
Use a second-pass human review for actions
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source, docs-only, and touches no data classes, so it does not create a residency or retention issue on its own. B is closed-source, vendor-hosted, and processes workspace pages through Notion backends, which can create policy mismatch if regulated content is placed there, but the profile does not show a specific prohibited class like PHI.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion workspace pages
IF the workspace policy forbids vendor-hosted processing of that data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI prompts
Use a separate compliant workspace
Review retention and export settings
Limit sharing to least-privilege users
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement
